# Daily Maintenance Workflow (`daily.yml`)

`daily.yml` groups the repository's recurring maintenance tasks. It handles
stale pull requests and, when GitHub Pages is enabled for the repository,
cleans up old documentation and checks it for dead links. It also prunes
obsolete GitHub Actions caches.

## Usage

Create `.github/workflows/daily.yml` in the consuming repository:

```yaml
name: Daily Maintenance

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 3 * * *' # Daily at 3am UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  daily:
    uses: eclipse-score/cicd-workflows/.github/workflows/daily.yml@main
    # Use this same caller-level group for documentation publication below.
    concurrency:
      group: docs-publish
      cancel-in-progress: false
      queue: max
```

## Coordinate with documentation publication

Daily cleanup and documentation publication both update `gh-pages`. If they
overlap, cleanup can change the branch after the publisher checks it out,
causing the publisher's push to fail with a non-fast-forward rejection.

Use the same job-level concurrency group in both calling workflows. The daily
caller above uses `docs-publish`; add the matching configuration to the job that
calls `docs-publish.yml` in your documentation workflow:

```yaml
jobs:
  publish:
    needs: build-docs # Use your documentation build job's ID.
    uses: eclipse-score/cicd-workflows/.github/workflows/docs-publish.yml@main
    concurrency:
      group: docs-publish
      cancel-in-progress: false
      queue: max
    # Keep the permissions and inputs required by your publication setup.
```

Concurrency groups are shared across workflows in a repository. Keep the group
identical for all callers that write `gh-pages`; do not include the workflow
name or triggering branch. Disabling cancellation lets an active writer finish,
and `queue: max` queues waiting jobs rather than replacing a pending run.

The publisher also has an internal `cicd-pages-deploy` concurrency group. That
group only serializes publishers; daily cleanup does not acquire it. Use a
different group name for the caller-level lock, as shown above, so a caller
does not hold the same lock its called workflow needs to acquire.

## Optional maintenance settings

The reusable workflow takes two optional boolean inputs, both default `false`:

- `skip-stale-prs`: disables stale pull request handling
- `skip-docs-link-check`: disables the documentation dead link check

For example, to keep documentation cleanup and cache pruning but skip stale
pull request handling:

```yaml
jobs:
  daily:
    uses: eclipse-score/cicd-workflows/.github/workflows/daily.yml@main
    with:
      skip-stale-prs: true
    concurrency:
      group: docs-publish
      cancel-in-progress: false
      queue: max
```

By default it applies a fixed maintenance policy:

- Marks pull requests as stale after `30` days of inactivity using the `stale` label
- Closes stale pull requests after `10` more days, adding the `autoclosed` label when closing
- Exempts pull requests labeled `keep-open`, `do-not-close`, `pinned`, or `feature_request`
- Runs documentation cleanup on the `gh-pages` branch when GitHub Pages is enabled
- Checks the documentation for dead links when GitHub Pages is enabled, using the
  [docs-as-code link check](https://github.com/eclipse-score/docs-as-code/tree/main/.github/actions/link-check).
  It runs `bazel run //:docs_link_check` and creates or updates an issue named
  "Automated Issue: Broken Documentation Links" listing what it found. The
  repository must provide the `//:docs_link_check` target (generated by
  docs-as-code); without it the check finds nothing and reports nothing
- Prunes obsolete GitHub Actions caches
